title: Automated screening of privacy risks in medical AI
abstract: arXiv:2610.30229v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Medical artificial intelligence (AI) models are often shared without their training data, assuming this protects the patients who contributed them. However, a model can reveal whether a patient's records were used in training, a privacy breach known as a membership inference attack. This risk is usually reported as a cohort average, which can appear negligible while individual patients are almost certainly exposed. Identifying potentially vulnerable records before developing a production model could make privacy assessment more practical. We measured each patient's vulnerability to membership inference attack, across 7,789 models trained on six clinical datasets in four modalities, including two adapted pretrained medical models. Training choices changed how many patients had high attack scores, but the patients who ranked highest by risk largely stayed the same across the configurations we tested. translated_title: 医疗AI中隐私风险的自动化筛查
translated_abstract: 医学人工智能（AI）模型通常在不附带训练数据的情况下被共享，并假定这样做可以保护贡献数据的患者。然而，模型可能会泄露某位患者的记录是否被用于训练，这种隐私泄露被称为成员推断攻击。这种风险通常以群体平均值的形式报告，这可能显得微不足道，而实际上个体患者却几乎肯定面临暴露风险。在开发生产模型之前识别潜在易受攻击的记录，可以使隐私评估更具实用性。我们测量了每位患者对成员推断攻击的脆弱性，共涉及在六种临床数据集、四种模态上训练的7,789个模型，其中包括两个适配的预训练医学模型。训练策略的选择会改变具有高攻击分数的患者数量，但在我们测试的各种配置中，按风险排名最高的患者群体基本保持不变。更强的权重衰减降低了暴露程度……
tldr: 该研究通过对7,789个医疗AI模型的患者级隐私风险分析，发现高风险患者排名在不同训练配置间基本保持稳定，从而可以在模型开发早期自动化识别和筛查易受成员推断攻击的脆弱患者记录。
en_tdlr: This study analyzes patient-level privacy risks across 7,789 medical AI models and finds that the highest-risk patients remain largely consistent across training configurations, enabling automated early screening of vulnerable patient records susceptible to membership inference attacks before production model development.
